title: Missing and Duplicate Receipts
description: A checkout service commits an order to PostgreSQL and then publishes an OrderPlaced event to a message broker; a worker emails receipts. Occasionally an order gets no receipt, and occasionally a customer receives two. Which design addresses both problems?

options.text: Publish the event first, then write the order to the database.
options.explanation: This reverses the failure: if the database write fails, a receipt is sent for an order that does not exist. Duplicates are not addressed.

options.text: Publish the event inside the database transaction so both roll back together.
options.explanation: A broker publish is not part of the database transaction. Rolling back the database does not unsend a message, and a commit failure after publishing still leaves an orphan event.

options.text: Put a cache in front of the database so the order write completes faster.
options.explanation: Speed does not change the fact that two independent writes can fail separately, and it does nothing for duplicate delivery.

options.text: Write the order and an outbox row in one transaction, relay outbox rows to the broker, and have the worker skip event IDs it has already processed.
options.explanation: The outbox makes the order and its event atomic, fixing missing receipts. The relay can publish twice, so an idempotent consumer keyed by event ID fixes duplicates.
